review_type: independent local source, runtime compatibility and public-package review

scope: Exact adjacent 18.04 to20.04 to22.04 to24.04 decisions, interrupted-stage holds and exact postboot target acceptance
Database major preservation, including refusal of implicit MySQL5.7 to8 migration
All installed legacy PHP extension packages protected during OS transitions and same-branch PHP package changes deferred
All five legacy source families map inventoried packages and builtin JSON without assuming PHP7.4
Multiple legacy branches, mixed active legacy and supported targets, removed embedded modules and pre-Noble migration are rejected
Full staged FPM then Nginx cutover for custom tenant pools and sockets across all five source families, preserving source bytes, INI directives and file modes
Exact retirement hook sets reject database or target removal, configuration actions and mismatched source proofs
Known PHP source pausing preserves Ubuntu entries, signing-key bytes, metadata and immutable originals; mixed deb822 failures occur before file mutation
Public allowlist, embedded twelve-module checksum/equality, release hashes, default modes, syntax and known private-identifier checks

actual_Python36_evidence.interpreter: CPython3.6.9 from Canonical-authenticated historical Ubuntu packages, privately extracted without installation
checks: Seven early modules compile and import under the actual old interpreter
Mocked Bionic plan chooses Focal with modern Node/PHP imports deferred
PHP stage rejects pre-Noble invocation before importing migration modules
No-op package-plan persistence and package logging exercised with a mocked child
Delivered verify_release.py passes under actual Python3.6 without executing the installer

findings_fixed: Python3.7-only timestamp API in the Bionic execution path
Custom non-www pool names not recognized by second-stage glob validation
limits: Local fixtures and mocked transactions do not establish live host compatibility or working recovery
Extracted Python3.6 runs on the test host kernel and does not reproduce the complete Bionic kernel or native APT environment
No complete native release transaction or live PHP application migration was executed
MySQL or other engine transitions that require a different database compatibility line intentionally hold
Multiple legacy branches, ambiguous/custom PHP layouts and unavailable or removed extension replacements require additional reviewed work
Static secret checks cannot guarantee absence of every possible secret; runtime-generated private evidence must never be published
The hashed host exclusion is not encryption or a guarantee against guessing
No universal production readiness, application compatibility or complete vulnerability-closure claim is made
